description:
Security researcher Quentin Kaiser has published a report regarding a 16-year-old bug that allows attackers to take control of various router models. The vulnerability lies deep within Broadcom software, potentially affecting millions of devices worldwide from well-known manufacturers like Asus, TP-Link, Netgear, Cisco, and Linksys—both consumer and business models.

The security vulnerability, known as WPSplinter, allows remote injection of malicious code and can lead to a takeover. It lies within Broadco
title: Millions of routers have a 16-year-old flaw that nobody plans to fix

description:
Last May, a close friend of mine died unexpectedly. He was 45, with no obvious warning signs that his brain was about to suffer a stroke.

The news was hard to take. I’d expected decades of friendship were still left. But even harder was making sense of his affairs. His family had no starting point of reference, and they lived states away. As one of the few close friends who lived nearby, I took the first crack at determining the logistics of his life: digital accounts, banking info, even his corporate equipment.

title: My friend died suddenly. I wish he’d taken these 4 steps for digital estate planning
